userStories.title: Resolve GitLab flow remotes to host-aware registered repos
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Introduce parseFlowRemoteUrl, use it in parseFlowInput and add host-aware GitLab repository lookup.

**Motivation** — Today every flow forge call mints a GitHub App token, so a flow on a GitLab repo is refused `fleet.flows.repoNotFound` (the remote URL parser accepts only github.com) or stopped `repo not connected` (`githubInstallationId === null`).

**Approach** — New `apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-remote-url.ts`:

**Interface** —
```ts
export type FlowRemote =
  | { provider: 'github'; owner: string; name: string }
  | { provider: 'gitlab'; url: string };
export function parseFlowRemoteUrl(url: string): FlowRemote;
```

Rules, in order:

1. A URL `parseGitHubUrl` accepts returns the `github` variant with its lowercased `owner` and `repo` (as `name`).
2. The URL must parse with `new URL`; its protocol must be `https:`; it must carry no username, no password, no query and no fragment; its hostname must not be `github.com` or `www.github.com` (a github.com URL rule 1 refused stays refused).
3. The path is normalised by removing one trailing `/`, then one trailing `.git` (case-insensitive). The normalised path must have at least two segments, none empty, `.` or `..`.
4. It returns the `gitlab` variant with `url` = `(origin + normalised path).toLowerCase()`.

Any URL failing rule 2 or 3 throws `ValidationAppException` `skills.unsupportedHost` (what `parseGitHubUrl` throws), so `parseFlowInput` reports `remoteUrl`.

New `FleetReposService.findGitLabByRemoteUrl(url: string): Promise<FleetRepoRecord | null>` backed by a new `IFleetRepoRepository.findGitLabByName(name: string): Promise<FleetRepoRecord[]>` (provider `gitlab`, name equal case-insensitively, ordered by `createdAt`, then `id`). The service keeps the first row whose `(host without trailing '/') + '/' + owner + '/' + name`, lowercased, equals `url`. A host with a path prefix therefore matches only URLs under that prefix, and the same path on another host never matches.

`parseFlowInput` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-input.ts:64-65`)
- Target: validates `remoteUrl` with the new `parseFlowRemoteUrl`; `normalized.remoteUrl` stays the input string.

GitLab rows store `owner` as the full namespace path (`group/sub`) and `host` as the origin plus any path prefix (`https://gitlab.com`, `https://example.com/gitlab`); `@@unique([provider, host, owner, name])`.

**Scope** — In: new parser and unit spec, switch only flow-input validation, extend repo domain interface/Prisma implementation/service, and create Postgres integration lookup spec. Verify real case-insensitive name queries, host isolation and prefix matching with shared DB helpers and canRunDbTests; run DB-backed spec outside sandbox via testScoped. No schema migration is required. Every existing test and contract file remains unchanged. Out: controller routing and reads (US-004), shared parseGitHubUrl changes, forge calls, and registration behavior. An ssh remote URL (`git@host:group/app.git`) stays refused for GitLab, as it is for GitHub.

userStories.title: Create NAX flows from GitLab repositories
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend FleetFlowsController.create to resolve GitLab remotes and verify head/specs with read credentials before approval.

**Motivation** — F1-F4a (merged #472-#475) made registration, jobs, reads and auto-review work on GitLab; flows are the last GitHub-only feature.

**Approach** — `FleetFlowsController.create` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/fleet-flows.controller.ts:73-121`)
- Target: `parseFlowRemoteUrl`; a `github` result keeps the baseline path; a `gitlab` result resolves the repo with `FleetReposService.findGitLabByRemoteUrl(url)`, runs the same project and permission checks, then reads the branch head and every spec through `call(repo, 'read', ...)`. Constructor gains `gitlabCredentials`, `gitlab` (appended). The `@ApiBody` `remoteUrl` description becomes `HTTPS github.com or GitLab repository URL`, and `openapi.json` is regenerated with `bun run api:export-spec` from the repo root.

**GitLab branch iff `repo.provider === 'gitlab'`.** A GitLab row takes the GitLab path whatever its `githubInstallationId` holds (a real GitLab row holds `null`), and never calls a `GitHubAppClient` method. The provider test comes before every `githubInstallationId === null` refusal; a GitHub row keeps today's code path unchanged, including those refusals.

**One `GitLabRepoCredentials.call` per GitLab client method call.** `call(repo, kind, fn)` marks the token invalid on a 401; wrapping a whole pass in one `call` would mark a token rotated mid-pass.

**New constructor dependencies are appended** after the existing ones: `GitLabRepoCredentials`, then `GitLabAccessChecker`. `GitBrokerModule` already exports both and `FlowsModule` (`flows.module.ts`) already imports it.

**Interface** — `GitLabRepoCredentials.call<T>(repo: { id: string; host?: string }, kind: 'read' | 'write', fn: (access: GitLabAccess) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` — `apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/gitlab-repo-credentials.ts`; throws `RepoCheckException('gitlab_credentials_missing')` for a repo with no credential row.
`FleetReposService.findGitLabByRemoteUrl(url: string): Promise<FleetRepoRecord | null>`; `parseFlowRemoteUrl(url: string): FlowRemote`; existing `getBranchHead(access, branch): Promise<string>` and `getFile(access, path, ref): Promise<ForgeFile | null>` remain the read interfaces.

Failure handling: Controller, GitLab: `gitlab_credentials_missing`, `gitlab_token_invalid`, `app_permissions_insufficient` → 409 `fleet.flows.gitlabNotConnected`; `repo_not_found` from the branch read → 409 `fleet.flows.branchNotFound`; `provider_unreachable`, `provider_error`, `vcs_encryption_key_missing` → 503 `fleet.flows.forgeUnavailable`; any other `RepoCheckException` reason → rethrown (422 `fleet.repoCheck`). Keep permission checks before every GitLab call and keep all reads before ApprovalRouteGate opens a transaction or persists its immutable input.

New API i18n key `flows.gitlabNotConnected.409` in `apps/api/src/i18n/en/fleet.json` ("Koda cannot read this GitLab repository: its tokens are missing or invalid; rotate them with koda fleet repo credentials") and `apps/api/src/i18n/zh/fleet.json` ("Koda 无法读取此 GitLab 仓库：其令牌缺失或无效；请使用 koda fleet repo credentials 轮换令牌").

**Scope** — In: controller GitLab path and new controller.gitlab.spec.ts; i18n keys; regenerate openapi.json with only remoteUrl description changed; extend flows.module.spec.ts StubGitBrokerModule to provide/export GitLabRepoCredentials and GitLabAccessChecker using useValue: {}, keeping every existing assertion. Production module already exports/imports the dependencies. Out: URL/repository implementation (US-003), advance/watch (US-005), calls/PRD/start write passes (US-006/007/008), hand-editing generated CLI files. GitHub path and existing controller specs remain unchanged.

userStories.title: Read GitLab flow heads and watch merge requests
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Route flow spec-head preflight, awaited merge-request reads and PR-number attribution to GitLab and classify missing/invalid GitLab credentials.

**Motivation** — F1-F4a (merged #472-#475) made registration, jobs, reads and auto-review work on GitLab; flows are the last GitHub-only feature.

**Approach** — `FleetFlowAdvanceService.readSpecHead` (`fleet-flow-advance.service.ts:794-812`), `prNumberOf` (`:898-906`)
- Target: a GitLab row reads the head through `call(repo, 'read', a => gitlab.getBranchHead(a, flow.branch))`; `prNumberOf` passes `provider: repo.provider === 'gitlab' ? 'gitlab' : 'github'` and `host: repo.host`, so a repo stub without `provider` (as the existing advance specs use) still parses GitHub PR URLs. Constructor gains `gitlabCredentials`, `gitlab` (appended); `featurePassDeps()` passes both.

`FeaturePassDeps` (`fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts:17`)
- Target: gains `gitlabCredentials: GitLabRepoCredentials` and `gitlab: GitLabAccessChecker`.

`runMergeWatch` / `pollAwaited` (`fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts:240-359`)
- Target: a GitLab row skips the GitHub mint and reads each awaited MR with `call(repo, 'read', a => gitlab.getMergeRequest(a, prNumber))`; the outcome rules (merged, closed, gone, retry, stop) are unchanged.

`callsOutcomeForForgeError` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-calls.ts:13`)
- Target: also `'failed'` for `gitlab_credentials_missing` and `gitlab_token_invalid`.

**GitLab branch iff `repo.provider === 'gitlab'`.** A GitLab row takes the GitLab path whatever its `githubInstallationId` holds (a real GitLab row holds `null`), and never calls a `GitHubAppClient` method. The provider test comes before every `githubInstallationId === null` refusal; a GitHub row keeps today's code path unchanged, including those refusals. The private helpers typed `githubInstallationId: bigint` (`createFeatureBranch`, `pollAwaited`) are called only for GitHub rows; GitLab rows get their own helpers.

**One `GitLabRepoCredentials.call` per GitLab client method call.** `call(repo, kind, fn)` marks the token invalid on a 401; wrapping a whole pass in one `call` would mark a token rotated mid-pass.

**New constructor dependencies are appended** after the existing ones: `GitLabRepoCredentials`, then `GitLabAccessChecker`. `GitBrokerModule` already exports both and `FlowsModule` (`flows.module.ts`) already imports it.

**Missing or invalid GitLab credentials stop a flow** where a GitHub App that is not installed stops it: `callsOutcomeForForgeError` classifies `gitlab_credentials_missing` and `gitlab_token_invalid` as `'failed'`. `vcs_encryption_key_missing` and the host refusals (`gitlab_host_blocked`, `gitlab_host_invalid`, `gitlab_host_unclassified`) keep the default `'retry'`: they are deployment or DNS faults an operator fixes, and the flow resumes on the next tick once fixed.

**The spec-head read stays a preflight hint.** `FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance` catches every `RepoCheckException` from `readSpecHead` and ends the pass without a write (`fleet-flow-advance.service.ts:589-594`); a GitLab repo keeps that rule, exactly as a GitHub one does. A flow whose token went bad is stopped only when a calls, PRD edits, start or watch pass reaches the forge and classifies the failure; a first-feature pass that only reads the spec head ends quietly each tick, as on GitHub.

**Interface** — `FeaturePassDeps` gains `gitlabCredentials: GitLabRepoCredentials` and `gitlab: GitLabAccessChecker`. `GitLabRepoCredentials.call<T>(repo: { id: string; host?: string }, kind: 'read' | 'write', fn: (access: GitLabAccess) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>`. `GitLabAccessChecker.getMergeRequest(access, iid): Promise<VcsPrStatus | null>`. `prNumberFor(repo: Pick<FleetRepoRef, 'provider' | 'owner' | 'name' | 'host'>, url)` — `apps/api/src/fleet/sync/pr-attribution.service.ts:27`; already parses GitLab MR URLs including a host path prefix.

**Scope** — In: advance constructor, spec head and PR-number mapping, featurePassDeps interface/factory, separate GitLab watch helper with existing observation/transaction semantics, classifier reasons, new fleet-flow-advance-gitlab.spec.ts driven through advance. flow-calls.spec.ts "marks known repository setup failures as failed" gains gitlab_credentials_missing and gitlab_token_invalid; "retries other forge failures" stays. Keep older GitHub specs and provider-less fixtures unchanged. Out: feature-start writes (US-008), calls and PRD writes (US-006/007), changing prNumberFor itself. US-005 only: a GitLab spec-head read failure does not stop the flow; the read is a preflight hint and the existing catch ends the pass with no write, as on GitHub.

userStories.title: Commit flow calls on GitLab with replay-safe locking
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the GitLab branch of FleetFlowCallsService.apply, preserving GitHub's existing algorithm and public outcomes.

**Motivation** — Today every flow forge call mints a GitHub App token, so a flow on a GitLab repo is refused `fleet.flows.repoNotFound` (the remote URL parser accepts only github.com) or stopped `repo not connected` (`githubInstallationId === null`).

**Approach** — Relevant target for `FleetFlowCallsService.apply` / `applyPrdEdits` / `isOwnEarlierCommit` (`fleet-flow-calls.service.ts:57-175`):
- Target: a GitLab row runs the same decision rules with `getBranchHead`, `getFileForUpdate` (pinned to the head), `commitFile` (with the file's `lastCommitId` as the lock), `isSingleFileCommit` and `isOwnCallsRun`. The base read (the file at `expectedHead`, or at `target.replay.reviewedHead` for a replay) is `call(repo, 'read', a => gitlab.getFile(a, path, baseHead))`, and an already-applied head is accepted only when its bytes equal the text built from that base AND the compare check passes, exactly as on GitHub. After a `conflict` the GitLab branch re-reads the file with `getFileForUpdate` on `target.branch` and compares `lastCommitId` (the lock it sent), not the blob sha: the same `lastCommitId` means nobody moved the file, so the branch refused the commit (`failed`); a moved file, a deleted file (null) or a re-read that throws a retry reason is `retry`. Constructor gains `gitlabCredentials`, `gitlab` (appended).

**GitLab branch iff `repo.provider === 'gitlab'`.** A GitLab row takes the GitLab path whatever its `githubInstallationId` holds (a real GitLab row holds `null`), and never calls a `GitHubAppClient` method. The provider test comes before every `githubInstallationId === null` refusal; a GitHub row keeps today's code path unchanged, including those refusals.

**One `GitLabRepoCredentials.call` per GitLab client method call.** `call(repo, kind, fn)` marks the token invalid on a 401; wrapping a whole pass in one `call` would mark a token rotated mid-pass.

**Token kind per request (design §5):** reads (`getBranchHead`, `getFile`, `getFileForUpdate`, `getMergeRequest`, `isSingleFileCommit`, `isOwnCallsRun`), including the re-read after a conflict, use `'read'`; writes (`createBranch`, `commitFile`) use `'write'`. `createBranch`'s own follow-up branch read runs inside the same `'write'` call, with the write token.

**New constructor dependencies are appended** after the existing ones: `GitLabRepoCredentials`, then `GitLabAccessChecker`. `GitBrokerModule` already exports both and `FlowsModule` (`flows.module.ts`) already imports it.

**Interface** — Preserve the existing `apply(flow: FleetFlowRecord, action: ApplyCallsAction, expectedHead: string, target: FleetFlowCallsTarget): Promise<CallsOutcome>` entry point. Consume these US-001/002 interfaces:

userStories.title: Commit GitLab flow PRD edits safely
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the GitLab path of FleetFlowCallsService.applyPrdEdits using lastCommitId locking and exact-byte single-commit recovery.

**Motivation** — F1-F4a (merged #472-#475) made registration, jobs, reads and auto-review work on GitLab; flows are the last GitHub-only feature.

**Approach** — Implement only the GitLab branch of `FleetFlowCallsService.applyPrdEdits` (`fleet-flow-calls.service.ts:57-115`). Read the branch head, then getFileForUpdate pinned to that head. The base read for moved-head recovery is `call(repo, 'read', a => gitlab.getFile(a, path, expectedHead))`; accept the head only if its bytes exactly equal applyPrdEditsToText applied to that base AND isSingleFileCommit proves the one-file direct-child commit. Like the GitHub path, PRD recovery uses isSingleFileCommit only.

After a `conflict` the GitLab branch re-reads the file with `getFileForUpdate` on `target.branch` and compares `lastCommitId` (the lock it sent), not the blob sha: the same `lastCommitId` means nobody moved the file, so the branch refused the commit (`failed`); a moved file, a deleted file (null) or a re-read that throws a retry reason is `retry`.

The constructor dependencies GitLabRepoCredentials then GitLabAccessChecker were appended in US-006 and must not be duplicated or reordered.

**GitLab branch iff `repo.provider === 'gitlab'`.** A GitLab row takes the GitLab path whatever its `githubInstallationId` holds (a real GitLab row holds `null`), and never calls a `GitHubAppClient` method. The provider test comes before every `githubInstallationId === null` refusal; a GitHub row keeps today's code path unchanged, including those refusals.

**One `GitLabRepoCredentials.call` per GitLab client method call.** `call(repo, kind, fn)` marks the token invalid on a 401; wrapping a whole pass in one `call` would mark a token rotated mid-pass.

**Token kind per request (design §5):** reads (`getBranchHead`, `getFile`, `getFileForUpdate`, `getMergeRequest`, `isSingleFileCommit`, `isOwnCallsRun`), including the re-read after a conflict, use `'read'`; writes (`createBranch`, `commitFile`) use `'write'`. `createBranch`'s own follow-up branch read runs inside the same `'write'` call, with the write token.

**Interface** — Preserve `applyPrdEdits(flow: FleetFlowRecord, action: ApplyPrdEditsAction, expectedHead: string, target: FleetFlowCallsTarget): Promise<PrdEditsOutcome>`.
```ts
getFileForUpdate(access, path: string, ref: string):
  Promise<(ForgeFile & { lastCommitId: string }) | null>
commitFile(access, path: string, input: { branch: string; content: Buffer; lastCommitId: string; message: string }):
  Promise<PutFileResult>
isSingleFileCommit(access, base: string, head: string, path: string): Promise<boolean>
```

Use `.nax/features/<feature>/prd.json` on target.branch. Read head and pinned update file separately through read credentials; build edits with applyPrdEditsToText and preserve applied/refused and unreadable/missing/empty-edit decisions. If applied === 0 return unchanged without a commit. If head moved, getFile at expectedHead through read credentials must yield base bytes whose edits exactly equal the head file AND the single-file compare must pass, otherwise stale. Commit through write credentials with message `chore(<feature>): flow PRD edits from PRD_REVIEW job <jobId>` and the update file's lastCommitId; return committed sha from commitSha plus applied/refused. Do not mutate flow state or hold a transaction over forge calls.

Failure handling: missing or invalid GitLab credentials return failed with the reason as detail; host refusal, encryption key missing and provider error return retry. commitFile 400/409 is conflict; unchanged lastCommitId on read-token reread returns failed detail `prd.json write refused`; moved/deleted file or retry-class reread error returns retry.

**Scope** — In: GitLab applyPrdEdits helper and new fleet-flow-prd-edits-gitlab.spec.ts. Out: calls implementation and constructor setup (US-006), client additions (US-001/002), feature start (US-008). Existing GitHub algorithm, tests and contract files stay unchanged. Sharing one forge-neutral implementation of the calls algorithm between GitHub and GitLab is not done: the GitHub path stays byte-for-byte as it is so its existing specs keep proving it. US-007 only: the own-commit check verifies linearity and the path, not the commit author, exactly as on GitHub. US-007 only: a GitLab push rule or protected-branch refusal of the PRD edits commit surfaces as `app_permissions_insufficient` and fails the pass; no separate `refused` mapping for a GitLab 403 is added.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] FleetFlowCallsService.applyPrdEdits on a GitLab repo { provider: 'gitlab', githubInstallationId: null } whose head equals expectedHead calls commitFile through call(repo, 'write', ...) with .nax/features/<feature>/prd.json, the edited text, the file's lastCommitId and message chore(<feature>): flow PRD edits from PRD_REVIEW job <jobId>, and returns { kind: 'committed', sha: <commitSha>, applied, refused }.
AC-2 [unit] When the GitLab prd.json has no edit to apply (applied === 0), applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'unchanged', refused } and never calls commitFile.

AC-3 [unit] When the GitLab head moved and isSingleFileCommit(access, expectedHead, head, '.nax/features/<feature>/prd.json') resolves false through call(repo, 'read', ...), applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'stale', head }.

AC-4 [unit] When the GitLab head moved, the file at the head equals the edits applied to the file read with getFile(access, path, expectedHead) through call(repo, 'read', ...), and isSingleFileCommit resolves true, applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'committed', sha: head, applied, refused }.
AC-5 [unit] When the GitLab head moved and isSingleFileCommit resolves true but the file at the head differs from the edits applied to the base file, applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'stale', head }.

AC-6 [unit] When commitFile returns { kind: 'conflict' } and the re-read with getFileForUpdate on target.branch has the same lastCommitId, applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'failed', detail: 'prd.json write refused' }.
AC-7 [unit] When commitFile returns { kind: 'conflict' } and the re-read has a different lastCommitId, applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'retry' }.
AC-8 [unit] When GitLabRepoCredentials.call rejects with RepoCheckException('gitlab_credentials_missing'), applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'failed', detail: 'gitlab_credentials_missing' }.
AC-9 [unit] For a GitLab repo row carrying githubInstallationId: 9n, applyPrdEdits never calls GitHubAppClient.mintInstallationToken.
Failure handling [unit] When GitLabRepoCredentials.call rejects with RepoCheckException('gitlab_token_invalid'), applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'failed', detail: 'gitlab_token_invalid' }.

Failure handling [unit] When a GitLab request rejects with gitlab_host_blocked, gitlab_host_invalid, gitlab_host_unclassified, vcs_encryption_key_missing or provider_error, applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'retry' }.
Failure handling [unit] When commitFile returns conflict and the read-token getFileForUpdate re-read returns null, applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'retry' }.
Failure handling [unit] When the conflict re-read rejects with a retry-class RepoCheckException, applyPrdEdits returns { kind: 'retry' }.

userStories.description:

**Motivation** — F1-F4a (merged #472-#475) made registration, jobs, reads and auto-review work on GitLab; flows are the last GitHub-only feature.

**Approach** — `runFeatureStart` / `createFeatureBranch` / `specMatchesApproved` (`fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts:77-163`)
- Target: a GitLab row reads the default-branch head and both spec blobs with the read token and creates the branch with `call(repo, 'write', a => gitlab.createBranch(a, branch, baseSha))`; the decision rules (`refused`, `exists` at the base, `exists` elsewhere) are unchanged.

**GitLab branch iff `repo.provider === 'gitlab'`.** A GitLab row takes the GitLab path whatever its `githubInstallationId` holds (a real GitLab row holds `null`), and never calls a `GitHubAppClient` method. The provider test comes before every `githubInstallationId === null` refusal; a GitHub row keeps today's code path unchanged, including those refusals. The private helpers typed `githubInstallationId: bigint` (`createFeatureBranch`, `pollAwaited`) are called only for GitHub rows; GitLab rows get their own helpers.

**One `GitLabRepoCredentials.call` per GitLab client method call.** `call(repo, kind, fn)` marks the token invalid on a 401; wrapping a whole pass in one `call` would mark a token rotated mid-pass.

**Token kind per request (design §5):** reads (`getBranchHead`, `getFile`, `getFileForUpdate`, `getMergeRequest`, `isSingleFileCommit`, `isOwnCallsRun`), including the re-read after a conflict, use `'read'`; writes (`createBranch`, `commitFile`) use `'write'`. `createBranch`'s own follow-up branch read runs inside the same `'write'` call, with the write token.

**Interface** — Consume upstream `FeaturePassDeps.gitlabCredentials: GitLabRepoCredentials` and `FeaturePassDeps.gitlab: GitLabAccessChecker`.
```ts
createBranch(access, branch: string, sha: string):
  Promise<{ kind: 'created' } | { kind: 'exists'; sha: string } | { kind: 'refused' }>
```

Preserve runFeatureStart's existing FeatureStartInput and FeatureStartOutcome interfaces. Resolve baseSha from defaultBranch when base === 'default', otherwise flow.setSha. Compare getFile blob shas at baseSha/setSha; missing or mismatched approved spec refuses spec_changed before any write. Keep the same-head optimization of one file read. Create feat/<feature>; exists at base is crash recovery, exists elsewhere stops dispatch_refused with `branch <branch> already exists`, refused stops dispatch_refused with `branch <branch> not created`. Only after forge work use existing recordFeatureStart to re-lock/recheck approval generation and write branch/state/audit/activity. Never hold DB transactions over HTTP. Missing/invalid credentials stop dispatch_refused with the reason as detail; host refusals, encryption key missing and provider errors retry next tick without writing.

**Scope** — In: separate GitLab branch creation/spec-matching helpers and new fleet-flow-feature-start-gitlab.spec.ts exercising FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance. Preserve every existing GitHub test and contract file. Out: client methods (US-001), FeaturePassDeps/advance constructor setup (US-005), calls and PRD edits (US-006/007). Thread-entry flows: they already run one feature on the thread's project repo, and threads on GitLab shipped in F3; nothing in this feature changes the thread entry.

AC-4 [unit] When createBranch returns { kind: 'refused' }, the start pass stops the flow with reason dispatch_refused and detail branch feat/b not created.
AC-5 [unit] When the spec blob sha at the base differs from the one at the set sha on a GitLab repo, the start pass stops the flow with reason spec_changed and never calls createBranch.

AC-6 [unit] When GitLabRepoCredentials.call rejects with RepoCheckException('gitlab_credentials_missing'), the start pass stops the flow with reason dispatch_refused and detail gitlab_credentials_missing.

AC-7 [unit] For each reason of provider_error and gitlab_host_blocked that createBranch rejects with, the start pass writes nothing and, when the fault is fixed and forge calls succeed, the feature is started on a later tick.

analysis:

Architecture and guidance: .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md is the API-specific authoring context. API owns persistence, permissions and workflow rules; no CLI, runner or web runtime changes are required.
